what_it_does: Logic synthesis is the automated process of translating a high-level chip description into an optimized network of basic logic gates. A key step is choosing the right sequence of rewriting transformations — each one rearranges part of the logic network to make it smaller or faster. Finding the best sequence is like finding the best order of moves in a board game: the space is astronomically large. Previous AI approaches (reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimization) struggled because the problem is fundamentally discrete — a sequence of named transformation steps — which is hard to optimize with smooth mathematical tools. This paper sidesteps that by using a diffusion model (the same family of AI that generates images from noise) to map discrete transformation sequences into a smooth continuous space, then uses gradient-based optimization (following the mathematical slope toward better solutions) guided by a learned predictor of the final chip quality, before mapping back to real transformation sequences.
